claim: For system (1.7) of Cao–Wang–Liu on \(\mathbb R_+^3\), assume \(A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4,B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4,C_1,C_2,C_3,K_1,K_2>0\), \(k_1,k_2\ge0\), \(0\le m_1,m_2\le1\), and \(q_iE_i\ge0\). Set \(R_1=A_1-q_1E_1\), \(R_2=B_1-q_2E_2\), \(M_1=K_1\max\{R_1,0\}/A_2\), \(M_2=K_2\max\{R_2,0\}/B_2\), \(D=C_3+q_3E_3\), and \(\Gamma=C_1(1-m_1)M_1+C_2(1-m_2)M_2-D\). If \(\Gamma<0\), then every compact invariant set is contained in the predator-free plane \(y=0\). Consequently every compactly supported invariant probability measure is supported on the equilibrium set of the predator-free planar competitive subsystem; in particular, no periodic, quasiperiodic, or chaotic compact recurrent dynamics can have positive predator density under this threshold.
integrity: The proof uses the printed deterministic system (1.7), exact sign inequalities, a complete-orbit compactness argument, Bendixson–Dulac on the predator-free plane, and Poincare recurrence. No numerical experiment is used as a proof of an infinite-time statement.
scientific_limitations: The threshold \(\Gamma<0\) is sufficient, not asserted necessary or optimal. It concerns compact invariant sets and compactly supported invariant probability measures, not arbitrary noncompact transients. The source's displayed chaotic parameter set lies outside the proved exclusion region.
title: A uniform predator-invasion ceiling excludes predator-positive compact recurrence
